terawulf-barker.note: I searched state air permit records, TeraWulf's 2025 annual report and 2026 results, county and press coverage. The campus buys grid power, with 90 MW from the state power authority, and the annual report mentions only temporary petroleum generators with no counts or ratings. I found no air permit and no generator or on-site gas plant. The site is the old Somerset coal plant, which is not in GEM's oil and gas tracker. It becomes an add if a permit names generators.

greenidge-generation-dresden.note: The only document is a March 2026 company announcement of 100 MW of grid power approval for data center expansion at the Dresden site. It names no generator or engine. The Greenidge gas plant that feeds the site is already in GEM as AES Greenidge power station.

digi-power-x-north-tonawanda.note: The only document is a Digi Power X announcement about its modular data center at North Tonawanda. It names no generator or engine. The Fortistar North Tonawanda gas plant on the site is already in GEM, owned by Digi Power X.

caithness-energy-llc-100-yaphank.note: The newest state air permit for Yaphank covers only the existing 346 MW plant. The Department of Energy request for information of April 2025 still describes a possible new 750 MW gas plant, which agrees with GEM. No permit, turbine maker or backup arrangement is on record, so nothing changes.
